units: scene/relative units only (NO mm, NO Myer-Cotton, NOT validation)

test1_cue.finding: near-light falloff cue EXISTS (monotone) but does NOT discriminate prox vs distal (profiles overlap, r60 ~equal)

test2_inverse_square.finding: WRONG ordering (proximal appears WIDER); stably wrong

test3_pretrained.finding: general (non-endoscopic) model: WRONG ordering AND unstable (distal CoV 63%); depth responds to FOV disk/bezel not tube geometry

DECISION: REVISED from NO-GO to CONDITIONAL: photometry is NOT dead. A STABLE, tube-geometry-consistent within-frame depth cue exists in d/dr log(B) (R^2 0.885, slope CoV 3%), reproducible across frames -- the raw brightness / cross-frame tests (1-3) missed it. But it is AGGREGATE-ONLY (per-direction texture-dominated) and BIASED (slope 0.75, wall flattening), so NOT directly usable: it needs angular aggregation + shading/vignetting calibration, and it has NOT been shown to resolve the actual narrowing. Recommend one more targeted test (does the calibrated aggregate cue track the known proximal<distal narrowing?) before building a photometric-geometric method.

test4_corrected_within_frame_gradient.method: radial d/dr log(B) (exposure-invariant), within-frame, scale-free shape vs tube 1/sin(alpha)
test4_corrected_within_frame_gradient.finding: CORRECTED test does NOT fail: angularly-averaged photometric depth follows tube geometry (R^2 0.885) with a STABLE biased slope (0.75, CoV 3%), reproducible across 8 neighboring frames. BUT per-direction angular consistency 0.34 (texture-dominated -> aggregate-only) and slope!=1 (needs shading/vignetting calibration).
